when: any static boost > +8 dB
text: That's a big boost. Big boosts usually mean something else is covering this sound. Try +2 to +4 dB, or cut the competing track instead.

when: a Bell boost with Q > 6
text: Narrow boosts tend to whistle. Rule of thumb: cut narrow to fix problems, boost wide to shape tone.

when: auto-gain off and output short-term loudness differs from input by more than 1.5 LU for 3 s
text: LENS is making this {louder|quieter} by {x} dB. Louder almost always sounds better to our ears, which fools us. Turn on auto-gain to judge honestly.

when: any band solo or detector Listen on for more than 15 s
text: Solo is for finding a problem. Judge the fix with solo off, with the whole mix playing.

when: a dynamic band at 0% activity for 10 s while input is above −50 dBFS
text: Band {n} isn't moving. The threshold is above anything it hears. Lower the threshold, or press Learn while the track plays.

when: a dynamic band above 90% activity for 10 s
text: Band {n} is moving almost all the time, so it's acting like a normal EQ. Raise the threshold so it only catches the loud moments, or make it a static band.

when: track type Bass or Kick & Drums, and a Low Cut above 45 Hz
text: That low cut is removing real bass. On bass and kick, cut only below the lowest note. A low E on bass is about 41 Hz; a five-string's low B is about 31 Hz.

when: track type Master, and a Low Cut above 35 Hz or steeper than 24 dB/oct
text: On the master, low cuts above about 30 Hz thin out the whole song. Keep master cuts low and gentle.

when: track type Master, and any static band beyond ±3 dB
text: Mastering moves are usually small: 0.5 to 2 dB. If you need more, the fix probably belongs in the mix.

when: output peak above 0 dBFS
text: The output is clipping. Turn output gain down, or turn on auto-gain.

when: Linear Phase on with track type Bass or Kick & Drums
text: Linear Phase can soften punch with pre-ringing: a faint swell just before each hit. Zero Latency usually sounds punchier on bass and drums.

when: the first time Linear Phase is switched on in a session
text: Linear Phase delays the audio by {ms} ms. Logic lines it up during playback, but don't record through it. If timing seems off, stop and restart playback.

when: a dynamic band below 150 Hz with release under 50 ms
text: A fast release on low frequencies can flutter or distort, because one bass wave lasts longer than that. Try 80–200 ms.

when: a band uses External detection and no side-chain signal arrives for 5 s while playing
text: This band listens to a side-chain, but nothing is arriving. In Logic, pick a track in the Side Chain menu at the top of the plugin window.

when: more than 10 bands on
text: That's a lot of bands. Try bypassing each one. If you can't hear the difference in the mix, delete it.

when: two boosting bands within 1/3 octave of each other
text: Two bands are boosting the same area. One band can do the job.

when: track type Vocal or Choir & Vocal Bus, a dynamic band between 4 and 10 kHz with attack over 10 ms
text: S sounds are over in a few milliseconds. For de-essing, an attack of 0.5–3 ms catches them.

when: a Side band on, and side level more than 40 dB below mid for 5 s
text: This track is basically mono, so Side bands have nothing to work on.

when: a boosting shelf with Q above 1.5
text: A high-Q shelf adds a bump near its corner. For smooth air or warmth, keep shelf Q around 0.5–0.8.

when: the first dynamic band of a session
text: Try Delta: you'll hear only what LENS is taking out. If you hear the music itself instead of the problem, you're cutting too much.

when: track type Master, the first time in a session
text: LENS goes before your limiter on the master. EQ first, then limit.
